mainEntity.name: How does a form builder actually sync with Google Sheets?

acceptedAnswer.text: The clean answer is a native integration. The form builder talks to Google's Sheets API, either creating a sheet for you or appending rows to one you pick. Apps Script and Zapier are the alternatives. Native is fastest; Zapier adds cost and a polling delay; Apps Script breaks when the API changes.

mainEntity.name: Which form builders sync to Google Sheets natively, without Zapier?

acceptedAnswer.text: Formester, Google Forms, Jotform, Paperform, Formstack, Fillout, Zoho Forms and Tally all offer native Google Sheets connectors in 2026. Typeform and Cognito Forms still route through Zapier or Make.

mainEntity.name: What is two-way Google Sheets sync, and which form builders support it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two-way means the form not only writes new submissions to the sheet but also reads from the sheet to populate fields. Fillout and Formester (via auto-fill from Sheets) handle this. Most others are one-way.

mainEntity.name: Why are my form responses not appearing in Google Sheets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three usual suspects: the connection token expired, the destination sheet was renamed or moved, or you added a new form field after the integration was set up and the columns no longer match.

mainEntity.name: Is there a free form builder with a real Google Sheets integration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Formester's free plan covers 100 responses/month with native Sheets sync. Fillout's free plan covers 1,000 responses. Google Forms is free with unlimited responses, capped by Drive storage. Tally's free plan covers unlimited forms with the native connector.

mainEntity.name: Does the form builder build the Google Sheet for me, or do I create it first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Native integrations (Formester, Google Forms, Jotform, Fillout) usually offer both: create a new sheet on connect, or pick an existing one and map fields. Zapier-based connections expect you to pre-build the sheet with column headers.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my Google Sheet when I delete the form?

acceptedAnswer.text: The sheet stays in your Drive. The form builder stops writing new rows, but historical responses are not erased.

mainEntity.name: How do I move my Google Forms responses to a different form builder without losing data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Export the linked sheet as CSV from Sheets. Import it into the new tool's response storage area. Rebuild the form, connect it to a fresh Google Sheet, and archive the old one.
